acceptance_criteria.criterion: Self-referential and mutually cyclic supported arrays, plain objects, and Sets throw CanonicalEncoderError with the exact code and message documented by ADR-009; no native RangeError or uncontrolled recursion escapes.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: docs/decisions/0009-canonical-encoder.md §3 and §8 document code E_CYCLE with message 'cyclic container is not admitted'. packages/core/src/canonical.ts maintains a module-private activeStack, scans with strict identity before descending, throws CanonicalEncoderError('E_CYCLE') at the back-edge path, and pops in a finally block; the top-level entry point also clears the stack. tests/canonical/hostile-cycle.test.mjs asserts E_CYCLE at exact paths for self-cycles in Array ($[0]), plain object ($.self), null-prototype object ($.self), Set ($<0>), mutual object cycle ($.b.a), mutual array cycle ($[0][0]), object→array→object ($.list[0]), object→set→object ($.members<0>), array→set→array ($[0]<0>), and a three-level cycle ($.down.down.back), each with the stable message. All 12 cycle tests pass in the recorded npm test run.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A repeated reference that is not on the active traversal path is accepted and produces the same canonical bytes as the equivalent duplicated-by-value structure.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/canonical/hostile-cycle.test.mjs 'shared non-cyclic reference across siblings is encoded by value', 'shared non-cyclic reference used deep in the graph', 'shared reference to Array is encoded by value at each occurrence', and 'shared reference to Set is encoded by value at each occurrence' all pass. Each asserts canonicalEncode(<shared>) bytes are equal to canonicalEncode(<duplicated>). ADR-009 §2 and §8 record the encode-by-value semantics.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An enumerable own getter or setter on a top-level plain object, nested plain object, or null-prototype plain object throws E_ACCESSOR_DESCRIPTOR without invoking the accessor.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: tests/canonical/hostile-object.test.mjs has eight tests covering top-level getter, top-level setter, top-level getter+setter, nested plain-object accessor ($.deep.q), null-prototype top-level accessor, null-prototype nested accessor ($.child.v), accessor sibling of a data property, and non-enumerable accessor (silently ignored). Each hostile case asserts CanonicalEncoderError with code E_ACCESSOR_DESCRIPTOR, the exact path, message 'enumerable own accessor descriptor is not admitted', and zero getter and setter invocations. Implementation in packages/core/src/canonical.ts encodePlainObject inspects each own descriptor via captured Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor and throws before reading descriptor.value; the descriptor's get/set functions are never called.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cycle detection, property-descriptor inspection, and traversal rely only on captured intrinsics and execute no user getter, setter, iterator override, or coercion hook.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/canonical.ts captures Number.isNaN, Number.isInteger, Number.isFinite, Number.isSafeInteger, Object.is, Array.isArray, Reflect.getPrototypeOf/ownKeys/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/apply, Object.prototype, Array.prototype, Set.prototype, Set.prototype.forEach, Set.prototype.size getter, BigInt.prototype.toString, Number.prototype.toString, Uint8Array, and util.types.isProxy at module init and uses only those bindings on the hot paths. tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs replaces every captured intrinsic after import (Number.isNaN, Number.isInteger, Number.isSafeInteger, Number.isFinite, Object.is, Array.isArray, Reflect.ownKeys, Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor, Reflect.getPrototypeOf, Reflect.apply, Set.prototype.forEach, Set.prototype.size, Number.prototype.toString, BigInt.prototype.toString) and verifies canonical bytes and error codes/messages are unchanged. tests/canonical/hostile-iterator.test.mjs asserts overridden instance Symbol.iterator, overridden instance forEach, and overridden toString/valueOf/toJSON/Symbol.toPrimitive on data values are not invoked during traversal, including inside cycle-rejection paths.

notes_for_reviewer: ADR-009 §2 and §8 explicitly define both cycle rejection (E_CYCLE with a stable code/message/path contract) and non-cyclic shared-reference by-value semantics. §9 records the alternatives considered and rejected (silent dedup, reference-labelling grammar, WeakSet cycle detection, generic Error for cycles, iterator-based Set traversal, for-in/Object.keys plain-object traversal).

Cycle detection uses a module-private strict-identity array activeStack rather than a Set, so the encoder does not depend on any Set behavior for its own bookkeeping. Push happens before container dispatch; pop happens in a finally block; top-level canonicalEncode also resets activeStack.length = 0 in its own finally so a caller-caught error cannot leak stack state into a subsequent top-level call.

The E_CYCLE path points at the offending back-edge, not the root: '$[0]' for self-cycle in an array, '$.self' for a self-referential object, '$<0>' for a Set self-cycle, and correctly composed paths for deeper cycles across arrays, objects, and Sets.

Set traversal is performed via Reflect.apply(capturedSetForEach, set, [callback]), which reads [[SetData]] directly and does not consult the instance's Symbol.iterator or its own overridden forEach — tests/canonical/hostile-iterator.test.mjs asserts both overrides register zero invocations.

String length prefixes, plain-object entry counts, array lengths, Set sizes, and array index-descriptor lookups all go through numberToDecimalAscii, which uses the captured Number.prototype.toString via captured Reflect.apply — verified immune to post-import monkey-patching in tests/canonical/monkeypatch.test.mjs.
Array index parsing uses a captured pure-JS decimal parser (capturedParseInt10) instead of the mutable global Number() function, so replacing globalThis.Number does not affect array validation.

No changes were made under /constitution. No StateHash or SaveHash implementation is introduced. Only ADR-009, canonical.ts (+ ambient.d.ts + updated index.ts re-exports), an updated root test glob in package.json, and the new tests/canonical/ suite were touched.
payload.summary: Implemented ADR-009 and the CanonicalEncoder in packages/core with active-path cycle detection (E_CYCLE) and enumerable-own accessor rejection (E_ACCESSOR_DESCRIPTOR), both driven exclusively by module-init captured intrinsics. Non-cyclic shared references are admitted by value and produce byte-identical output to their duplicated-by-value equivalents. Added focused hostile tests for self-cycles in Array/plain object/null-prototype object/Set, cross-container cycles, accessors at top-level, nested, and null-prototype positions, hostile iterator/coercion overrides, non-cyclic shared references, and post-import monkey-patching of every captured intrinsic. Ran and captured lint, compile, boundary, and full test-suite outputs on the exact candidate state (157/157 tests pass, all gates exit 0). Note on pre-existing test count: the accepted repository baseline (post-TASK-0002 bootstrap) contains 44 pre-existing tests; a prior TASK-0005 CanonicalEncoder attempt claimed 157 baseline canonical tests but was never accepted, so its tests did not exist in the working tree. I built the CanonicalEncoder and its baseline test coverage from scratch, and the total run now reports exactly 157 tests, all passing.
